title: Should you learn to code in 2027?
summary: A clean, fluent take: no "scratch that", one restart on the opening statistic, and no pause over 1.2 s inside her speech. The file starts at her first word (0.6 s) and has 1.2 s of room tone at the end.

cuts.why: She says the statistic, then starts it again: "…in the first quarter of 2026, only 4.5%. And that's in the first quarter, only 4.5% of software development job postings…". Keeps one clean sentence: "…in the first quarter of 2026, only 4.5% of software development job postings on Indeed were entry level."

decisions:
- **0:44 "So the job postings are mostly for senior roles. Senior roles, yeah."**: an emphasis repeat; keep or cut 44.4 to 45.4 by ear (not counted).
- **1:28-1:37 "…it was so easy. Now I'm realizing how easy it was, because then I was like, oh my God, it was so hard! When I'm like, oh my God, it was so easy."**: a bit tangled but it's her joke; left in.
- **6:23-6:40 ending**: she ends on "…I don't think that is a promise you want to hold so seriously." No sign-off and no call to action; the kit didn't have a strong one either.
- Optional tightening: the two pauses at 0:59-1:01 ("…then this video is for you. ⟨0.7 s⟩ Because ⟨0.9 s⟩ I know you're probably asking yourself") could go to 0.4 s each.
kit:
**Skipped from the kit:**
- "Senior roles made up 71 percent of the increase from May 2025 to May 2026" (on-screen card can still carry it).
- The definition of vibe coding ("when you describe what you want and let AI write the code, without really reading it").
- "At my job, I barely write code by hand anymore. What I do is understand the code, and monitor what it's doing."
- "So as the human in the loop of using AI to code, you need that" (shortened to "you add the human in the loop").
- The story about her manager ("When I first got my job … my manager would always refer me back and say, oh yeah, no, you cannot do that. Because he had more context").
- The kit's closing question ("So should you still learn to code in 2027? I still think you should try…") is said in looser words.

**Added:** "Someone I know is really, really interested in being a software developer right now … that was even what led me to recording this video"; "AI is really good at debugging as well, and I'm not even joking"; "Everybody using AI to write code, I promise you that"; "I'll try to add some links in the description box" (free places to learn system design and fundamentals: the description needs those links).

**Facts to check:**
- 0:15 Indeed Hiring Lab: 4.5% of software development postings entry level in Q1 2026 ✓ kit.
- 0:38 "in the US, about 15% between February last year to June this year": ✓ kit (February 2025 to June 2026). "last year / this year" only reads right if posted in 2026.
- She says "I write code for a fleet management company" (matches her job; fine to keep).
